brief: War report. Cold, clipped, present tense — a correspondent filing from somewhere with a deadline, not a host explaining. Same register as the house narrator in one respect only: it never sells. The difference is temperature. The house voice is measured and warm; this one is measured and cold, and it does not soften a number by the way it says it.

primary.why: Deep, natural, articulate US male — the same catalogue entry the house kit uses, and the ONLY voice measured end to end on this stack (six CS-1 takes, ffprobe on the trimmed files).
primary.why_not_a_colder_voice: A war-report read wants a harder, more clipped voice than this, and the honest answer is that no such voice has been measured here. A voice_id that is not in this account resolves to nothing at render time: the narration stage fails on a 404 after the pictures are already paid for, or — worse on some adapters — falls back to a provider default, which is a different narrator with the manifest still naming this one (see narration._spec, which refuses exactly that). So the kit ships the voice that is known to work, and the war-report register is written down in `direction` below for the human who casts the next one. Casting a colder narrator is a change to make WITH a measurement, not instead of one.
primary.direction: NOT SENT TO THE PROVIDER. `narration.voice_specs` builds a request from provider, model and voice_id only; no module reads this field. It is the casting note — what to listen for when a harder voice is auditioned, and what the script's phrasing is already aiming at. Recorded rather than wired, because a field that looks like an instruction and reaches nothing is worse than no field: cold, level, present tense; short declaratives; no lift at the end of a sentence and no warmth on the kicker; let the pauses do the work, since the sentence-end pause is what fills the window on this model, not extra words.
primary.model_note: Direct ElevenLabs, not routed through GMICloud — 'ElevenLabs-TTS-v3' is the GMI slug and is rejected here.

fallback.why: Narrative-classified, calm, US male. Nearest tonal match on the fallback provider, and the fallback the house kit already measured.
fallback.note: A fallback voice will never match the primary. That is disclosed rather than hidden: the manifest records which provider voiced each block and the receipt shows it. A visible substitution is more honest than a silent one.
fallback.lmnt_pads_heavily: The CS-5 sabotage run measured LMNT emitting up to 28.7s of trailing silence on one block. Silence is stripped before the take is measured; without that, one block would have been forty seconds long in the assembly.

why_the_window_moved.what_happened: The first diorama run was voiced and measured. Six takes on stories/diorama-smoke.yaml, this voice_id on eleven_v3, every line inside POL-5's 23-27 word window: 9.888, 11.242, 9.438, 11.704, 10.320, 10.725s. Three of six fell outside 9.0-10.5, all by running long, and an out-of-window take is not a warning — `narration.run_take` marks it `review`, `Take.ok` is False, and the narration stage FAILED the run: '$0.277 spent, blocks 2, 4, 6 were not voiced'. The takes were not wrong and neither were the lines. The window was.
why_the_window_moved.why_9_0_stays: Unchanged, and not by inertia. The observed minimum is 9.438s, so 9.0 still has 0.44s of clearance below a normal read, and a take under it is the ONE failure the correction ladder can actually reach — [pause] tags lengthen a short take and nothing lengthens time in the other direction.
why_the_window_moved.why_12_5: Derived from these six takes twice over, and both derivations land in the same place. (1) The observed band is 9.438-11.704s; 12.5 clears the longest normal take by 0.8s, which is about mean + 2.3 standard deviations on this sample — outside the natural spread of a compliant read rather than inside it, which is what an uncorrectable failure mode requires. (2) The measured rate ran 2.14-2.65 w/s. A POL-5-maximum 27-word line at the slowest observed rate is 27/2.14 = 12.6s. So the check can still fail on a line POL-5 admits, by a small margin, which is the property the house file argues for: a window that cannot fail is worse than one that fails too often.
why_the_window_moved.why_not_the_houses_13_0: Because copying it would be inheriting a correction this kit did not earn. The house moved to 13.0 against takes reaching 12.56s; ours reach 11.704s. Setting 13.0 here would buy 1.3s of slack no measurement asked for and would quietly stop catching the long read it is supposed to catch.
why_the_window_moved.the_honest_caveat: Six takes, one story, one narrator. It is a runtime budget, not a law. A second diorama story should read these numbers as the starting point they now are, and re-measure if its takes drift.
why_the_window_moved.what_this_cost: $0.277 and a failed narration stage, which is the cheapest place this could have been discovered — text and audio, before any video was bought.

why_this_window_was_9_0_to_10_5.SUPERSEDED: By why_the_window_moved above, on the same day, by the first six measured takes. Kept because this repo keeps the wrong version next to the right one — and because this one got its own prediction right, which is the useful part: it said the number was an intention rather than a measurement, said what would happen if it were trusted, and said to re-measure rather than widen. That is exactly what happened and exactly what was done. A note that names its own weakness is why the failure cost $0.277 and a stage rather than a re-rendered video.
why_this_window_was_9_0_to_10_5.what_this_number_is: The reference brief's target for this style — a clipped ten-second beat, six of them, a piece around sixty seconds. It is an intention. It has not been measured on a diorama story.
why_this_window_was_9_0_to_10_5.the_correction_it_must_not_repeat: The house kit started at exactly these numbers and moved to 9.0-13.0 on 2026-07-28, after six CS-1 blocks were voiced and measured at 9.25, 9.28, 9.64, 10.88, 12.40 and 12.56s. Three of six fell outside a 9.0-10.5 window, all by running long, and an overrun has NO correction on this stack: the genblaze ElevenLabs adapter builds voice_settings from stability, similarity_boost and style only and never forwards speed. The house file's own closing caveat is the instruction here — 'a second story on a different voice should re-measure rather than inherit these numbers'.
why_this_window_was_9_0_to_10_5.so_what_happens_on_the_first_run: Expect blocks flagged `review` for running long, and read that as this window being untested rather than as the takes being wrong. A flag does not fail the run; POL-5 is a runtime budget, not a sync constraint (§6.6). Re-measure from the first six diorama takes and move this number with the measurement written beside it, the way the house window records its own move. Do not widen it on a hunch, and do not narrow the script to defend it — regenerating the script changes the lines, which invalidates every take already cut from them.
why_this_window_was_9_0_to_10_5.one_thing_this_got_wrong: 'A flag does not fail the run.' It does. An out-of-window take is marked `review`, `Take.ok` returns False on anything but `ready`, and `stage_narration` reports the block as not voiced and stops the run. POL-5 being a runtime budget rather than a sync constraint is true of the DESIGN and not of this code path. Read as advice it was reassuring and wrong; the run stopped with three blocks paid for and unusable.
why_this_window_was_9_0_to_10_5.why_it_is_not_simply_set_to_the_house_nu: Because the house number was measured on a warm documentary read of house-length sentences, and this kit asks for a colder, more clipped one. Inheriting 13.0 would carry over a correction that was earned by a different delivery. The window a style should start from is its brief; the window it keeps is the one its takes measure.

delivery.why_not_one_flowing_sentence: Imported vox guidance says to prefer single flowing sentences because they run fast and overrun. On eleven_v3 the opposite held: flowing lines came back SHORT and it was the sentence-end pauses that filled the window. The only one of four calibration takes that landed in window was the choppy one — 22 words across five sentences. Clipped war-report phrasing is therefore doing two jobs here, register and runtime, which is the one place this kit and the house measurement agree without argument.
delivery.duration_must_be_measured: asset.duration comes back None from the ElevenLabs adapter, so POL-5 cannot read it from the manifest. Take length is measured with ffprobe on the downloaded file, after trailing silence is stripped. Word count is a coarse pre-flight bound only.
correction_order: lengthen with [pause] tags at internal sentence boundaries — about 0.36s each, and the only lever that leaves the journalist's words alone
[long pause] buys about 1.25s where a beat is wanted anyway; [short pause] was dropped from the ladder because it was there by symmetry and never by measurement
flag for human review after two attempts. An overrun has no correction at all — say so rather than burning renders on it
delivery.do_not_voice_six_blocks_at_once: Six concurrent ElevenLabs calls returned code=rate_limit and pushed four of six blocks onto LMNT — a narrator change we caused ourselves, recorded as though the provider had failed. Two at a time.

tail_by_role._why: Tighter than the house across the board, because the register is a filed report rather than an essay and air between beats reads as hesitation here. The shape is the same six-beat one: a long breath after the cold open so the number lands, tight between the two evidence beats because they are one argument, air before the kicker, and the longest gap after it because that one is the outro. No two values are equal — evenly spaced gaps are the first of the four things that make an explainer feel machine-made.
tail_by_role._offset_why: The formula spends two consecutive blocks on 'evidence', which would give them the same tail and put two identical gaps in a piece with only five. The second runs 0.15s longer — still tight, still inside the range, no longer a duplicate.

assembly_contract.measure_with: ffprobe on the downloaded file — asset.duration is None from the ElevenLabs adapter
never: speed-compress the voice to fit a window
stretch or squeeze video to fit audio
centre a take inside a fixed block
assembly_contract.why: Audio leads and picture follows. Block length is derived from the take (lead-in + take + tail), the clip is trimmed or its last frame held to match, and the voice is never speed-compressed. 0.4s of lead-in is the beat a viewer needs to read a new image before a voice starts — and on this style the image is doing more work than usual, so the lead-in is the last thing to cut.

delivery.pol5_role: A RUNTIME BUDGET, not a sync constraint. Six takes near ten seconds keeps the piece around sixty. A take outside the window makes the story longer or shorter than intended; it no longer desyncs anything.
